chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithamī, from Anbasa Al-ʿĀbid, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Joking is the smallest insult.'

key_terms.الْمِزَاحُ: Joking, playful banter, or lighthearted speech

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or social status of joking in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from al-Kāfī, Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) identifies playful joking (al-mizāḥ) as 'al-sibāb al-aṣghar' (the minor insult), linking it to the broader Islamic legal concept of *sibāb* (verbal abuse or cursing). This classification underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette), warning that even lighthearted banter can constitute a subtle form of demeaning another if it crosses into slighting or mockery, thereby requiring mindfulness in social interactions.
